BD_FEE_FIELD_IS_FLOW.cause: BD's `fees` equals minus its `netAdditions` and the money gain (ending - beginning - net additions) is about zero: the contribution is booked through the fee field and BD's TWR reads it as a return, so the fee add-back and the TWR are both of a flow, not of a fee or a gain.
BD_FEE_FIELD_IS_FLOW.note: fix = `landed_gain_return()` below: grade such a segment on BD's own landed values, (ending - beginning - net additions) / mean daily served value, not on the TWR; the re-graded effect on this class is in `regrade_effect.BD_FEE_FIELD_IS_FLOW.within_landed_gain`. The reader of record is not edited.

FIRST_DAY_FLOW_AT_START.cause: a flow on the segment's first day is invested for that day in BD (START timing), where the served END convention leaves it uninvested.
FIRST_DAY_FLOW_AT_START.note: fix = START timing on the first-day flow (`relink(..., 'START', {0})`); lands all rows of the class; the flow-start convention of DB-b-61 reaches the same rows. Effect outside these 170 is not measured here.

FLOW_DAY_RETURN_ZERO.cause: BD earns nothing on the large flow day (its per-flow valuation is not in the landed period point); Opal's own return on that day carries the miss. Setting the day's return to zero lands every row, which names the day, not BD's rule.
FLOW_DAY_RETURN_ZERO.note: not adopted: START, MID and a one-day move each also land some of these rows, so the landed files cannot tell the rules apart.

FLOW_START_OR_MID.cause: START or MID timing on the large flow days lands the row; BD's flow date is not landed, so no date is adopted (as round 31's FLOW_TIMING).
FLOW_START_OR_MID.note: graded both ways by DB-b-59; the flow-start adoption of DB-b-61 is the reader-of-record question.

FLOW_BOOKED_A_DAY_APART.cause: moving the large flow one day later (the other system books it the next day) lands the row; BD's booking date is not landed.
FLOW_BOOKED_A_DAY_APART.note: evidence is the re-link that lands, not a landed BD date; not adopted.

LIQUIDATION_RESIDUAL_BASE.cause: a large outflow leaves under 5% of the prior value; the rest of the segment compounds on a residual base, and BD's valuation of the emptying day and of the tail is not in the landed period point. No re-link tested lands these rows.
LIQUIDATION_RESIDUAL_BASE.note: tested and not landing: START, MID, flow-day zero, a one-day move either way, link cut at the last large flow.

FUNDED_FROM_NEAR_ZERO.cause: a large inflow lands on a prior value under 5% of the post-flow value (an account opened or funded from a near-zero base); the return before and on the funding day is set by cents of value and BD's per-flow valuation is not landed.
FUNDED_FROM_NEAR_ZERO.note: no re-link tested lands these rows.

ROUND_TRIP_FLOWS.cause: opposite-sign large flows within five served days net to under 10% of the larger (money out and back); each leg's valuation in BD is not in the landed period point.
ROUND_TRIP_FLOWS.note: no re-link tested lands these rows.

MULTI_FLOW_COMPOUNDING.cause: three or more large flow days compound their valuation differences; no single flow is the cause and BD's per-flow valuation is not landed.
MULTI_FLOW_COMPOUNDING.note: no single-cause re-link tested lands these rows.

SINGLE_PARTIAL_FLOW.cause: one or two partial large flows (neither emptying nor funding the account); BD's per-flow valuation is not in the landed period point and no re-link tested lands the row.
